facts.claim: Amy Lee's "With or Without You" is a cover of U2's song, which first appeared on their 1987 album The Joshua Tree.
Lee released the cover through her newly launched YouTube channel in November 2015, as her second cover video there.
The cover follows her first cover in the series, Portishead's "It's a Fire".

Rolling Stone described the arrangement as a dark, synth-heavy, minimalist industrial take on the arena-rock original. Its black-and-white video shows Lee posing by foliage and recording in her home studio.
Lee said the dark version was playing in her head as she woke up one morning. She then went straight upstairs and laid down the synth and basic vocal.
Lee said she saw U2 live at Madison Square Garden in 2015, that it made her excited to play live again, and that this is still her favorite U2 track.
Lee said love is rarely simple and is more often tearing your guts out, which is why the song haunts her dreams.
mxdwn noted that Lee swapped the piano and strings of the original for heavy synth and put the emphasis on the lyrics.
The track was later included on Lee's covers EP Recover, Vol. 1, released February 19, 2016, which has four covers and videos directed by Eric Ryan Anderson.
Lee is the frontwoman of Evanescence, and the cover was part of a YouTube channel created to showcase her solo work.

research.lineage: A dark, synth-driven industrial reworking of a 1987 U2 arena-rock ballad, issued as part of Amy Lee's solo covers series after her work with Evanescence.

draft:
**With or Without You** has always been a song about a bind, and Amy Lee strips it down until the bind is all that's left. A low synth pad hums underneath like something left running in an empty room. A clean electric guitar picks out arpeggios. The drums keep a slow ballad pace, kick and snare landing with weight, all of it soaked in reverb so the space feels huge and cold. Rolling Stone heard it as a minimalist, industrial take on an arena-rock original. That is the right frame. U2's 1987 version, from *The Joshua Tree*, swells toward release. Lee's leaves the walls up.

The swap matters. Lee traded the piano and strings of the original for heavy synth and pushed the lyrics to the front. Her voice is clear and strong and held long on the vowels, with a slight vibrato and no harmonies to soften it. Nobody joins in. That loneliness is the point, because the song describes a person caught between two kinds of pain. "I can't live / With or without you" is not a romantic flourish here. It sounds like a diagnosis.

The writing holds more than one feeling at once, and the cover lets them sit unresolved. "On a bed of nails she makes me wait" brings in a third figure and turns patience into punishment. Then comes the line that gives the narrator away: "You give it all, but I want more." There's grievance in it, and also an ugly, honest admission that nothing would be enough. The refrain, "And you give yourself away," cuts in both directions. It could be an accusation or a lament for someone erasing themselves, and the repetitions trail off into "And you give…" as if the sentence can't be finished. The middle section reads like a body counting its damage: hands tied, bruised, "nothing left to lose."

Lee has said love is rarely simple and more often tears your guts out, which is why the song stays with her. She saw U2 at Madison Square Garden in 2015, called this her favorite of their tracks, and came away wanting to play live again. Then the dark version arrived in her head one morning as she woke up. She went straight upstairs and laid down the synth and a basic vocal. It became the second cover on her new YouTube channel, a home for her work outside Evanescence, after Portishead's "It's a Fire." The black-and-white video shows her by foliage and at work in her home studio, and it was later collected on the *Recover, Vol. 1* EP.

What sticks is the refusal to let the chorus lift you out of the trap, so you stay inside that cold, echoing room with someone who can neither leave nor stay.
